title: A1 adaptation falsification: asymmetry, confidence and carryover tests
research_question: If the A1 adapter PPP lift is real coverage response, wrong-way teams should do worse than no-signal teams, the gap should widen with scheme-vote confidence, and adapting in Game N should carry over to Game N+1.
original_hypothesis: If the A1 adapter PPP lift is real coverage response, wrong-way teams should do worse than no-signal teams, the gap should widen with scheme-vote confidence, and adapting in Game N should carry over to Game N+1.
datasets_and_fields: NBA play-by-play possessions and reconstructed lineups; Playoff series outcomes
design_as_recorded: Playoff possessions only; game-team cells bucketed adapter/neutral/no_signal/wrong_way; early-to-late third PPP deltas; 430 consecutive (N, N+1) series pairs; one-sided Welch and Mann-Whitney tests.
primary_result: T1 dPPP: adapter +0.0667 (n=205), neutral +0.0248 (n=50), no_signal +0.1260 (n=57), wrong_way +0.0111 (n=274). T2: adapter minus no-signal -0.0361 (1 vote), -0.1170 (2 votes). T3 next-game PPP Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842; MW p=0.863; counter-carry Welch t=-2.163, p=0.985.
failure_evidence: no_signal bucket (+0.1260) beats adapters (+0.0667); gap does not widen with confidence; carryover p=0.84; follow-up showed buckets selected on extreme early-third PPP (regression to mean).
power_or_reliability_limitations: n=205/50/57/274 cells; 430 pairs | categories: selection or regression to the mean; label or classification error
confounds_leakage_or_implementation_prob: no_signal bucket (+0.1260) beats adapters (+0.0667); gap does not widen with confidence; carryover p=0.84; follow-up showed buckets selected on extreme early-third PPP (regression to mean).
notes: Scheme labels are only assigned when early-third PT PPP is >=10% hot/cold, which mechanically builds in mean reversion; this selection was knowable from the labeling rule before outcomes.
